title: M0 go/no-go decision for pluggable cognitive memory providers
decision: Proceed with a capability-based provider boundary above existing TraceDecay Native application ports. Do not replace TraceDecay authorities, Native fact-store contracts, repository/worktree identity, session evidence, host integration, or final context ownership.
m1_release_condition: M1 remains blocked until tdmem-0107 is closed by the automated Beads operation after the report contract tests and repository validator pass.

evidence.finding: The product branch descends from immutable PR #707 floor 08fbe33a7c7f403191fd5d6e356c7b6681b96403.

GitHub Actions run 33299093667 completed the clean V2 build plus focused memory, retrieval, host, daemon, dashboard, generated-drift, and working-tree checks; receipt commit b391cd32ba51e5a8ad584740073554476bca5d8c records the run.
Production write, read/recall, feedback, maintenance, inspection, host-injection, CLI, MCP, SDK, dashboard, hooks, automation, store, and test paths are mapped to concrete owners and seams.
Every durable domain has one canonical writer; provider state and recall remain separate advisory authorities.
Additive product-owned work is preferred; existing upstream-file edits have hard quantitative caps, allowed mounts, forbidden zones, and convergence-map requirements.
At the M0 decision point no Zack-owned existing production or test file is intentionally modified by product implementation.
Eight binding decisions cover provider boundaries, authority, crate layout, execution topology gate, persistence/recovery, context compilation, observer isolation, and upstream convergence.

selected_insertion_points.selection: Define the provider-neutral protocol and capability vocabulary before any concrete adapter. Mount only typed provider-neutral application ports later; never implement ProjectMemoryFactStore for an external provider.

Construct one capability-driven registry at project startup, bind exact project, worktree, provider-instance and mode identity once, and inject provider-neutral lifecycle ports. Concrete provider logic remains outside the composition root.
Fan out only after canonical host-neutral admission or settlement into a bounded durable product-owned dispatcher. Observer latency and failure cannot affect the canonical result.

Request bounded advisory candidates through capability ports, then apply exact-scope, freshness, provenance, privacy, deadline, cancellation and deterministic budget admission before TraceDecay assembles final context.
Emit idempotent provider feedback only after canonical settlement. Provider failure must remain an isolated typed dispatch outcome and cannot rewrite Native trust or the settled operation.

first_slice.title: Provider capability registry contract
first_slice.goal: Define stable provider-neutral mandatory and optional capability identifiers, operation semantics, typed failure classes, compatibility rules, and unknown-capability round-trip behavior without creating or selecting a concrete provider adapter.

crates.reason: M1 fixes the transport-neutral contract authority first; M2 creates and wires the Rust crates after the contract is executable-validated.

acceptance: Mandatory and optional capabilities are separate and capability identifiers never encode implementation names.
Every capability declares operations, inputs, outputs, typed failure modes and compatibility behavior.
Unknown well-formed capabilities round-trip as inactive opaque declarations and cannot activate behavior.
The first slice changes no existing upstream-owned file and creates no concrete provider adapter.

go_reasons: The provider boundary can be mounted above existing application/use-case ports rather than replacing ProjectMemoryFactStore or DatabaseFactStore.

TraceDecay already exposes exact owner/scope, deadlines, cancellation, provenance, typed terminal outcomes, idempotent commands, durable receipts, and recovery seams that can constrain provider adapters.
Native behavior can first be adapted and parity-tested behind the same provider-neutral contract before NCM influences any agent context.
Observer delivery can be isolated after canonical settlement through a bounded durable outbox, so provider failure need not affect product behavior.
The patch-footprint policy permits narrow composition/application mounts while keeping product crates additive and independently removable.

residual_risks.risk: Native fact-store semantics could leak into the provider API and exclude cognitive providers.
residual_risks.mitigation: Define capability-oriented contracts and prove them with dummy-provider conformance before concrete adapters.

residual_risks.risk: Routing Native through the new boundary could change outputs, receipts, errors, or recovery behavior.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep the direct path as the oracle and require golden parity before default cutover.

residual_risks.risk: Crashes around provider commit/acknowledgement could duplicate or lose observations.
residual_risks.mitigation: Use stable idempotency, durable bounded journal state, typed partial effects, receipts, replay, and crash injection.

residual_risks.risk: Stale, cross-worktree, revoked, sensitive, or injection-like provider content could enter an agent context.
residual_risks.mitigation: Keep TraceDecay-owned exact-scope admission, temporal/revocation checks, deterministic budgets, evidence formatting, and explain traces.

residual_risks.risk: Observer output, latency, or failures could accidentally alter prompts or canonical outcomes.
residual_risks.mitigation: Use a result-unreachable observer route and compare output/state hashes across healthy and failing observers.

residual_risks.risk: The licensed NCM implementation may not support the assumed API, lifecycle, persistence, or deployment topology.
residual_risks.mitigation: Audit the licensed surface first and select topology only through the explicit decision-gate ADR.

residual_risks.risk: Provider mounts could make future PR #707 successor syncs conflict-heavy or semantically unsafe.
residual_risks.mitigation: Enforce additive ownership, convergence entries, hard caps, isolated sync trains, conflict receipts, and parity gates.

deferred_decisions.reason: The licensed surface has not yet been audited.
No versioned OCEAN provider specification is available; only a provider slot is reserved.
Initial delivery selects one explicit active provider; cross-provider blending requires separate authority, scoring, and failure-policy evidence.

implementation_order.name: Product-owned crate skeletons, dependency guards, and composition mount
Durable observation dispatch and provider lifecycle
Provider recall admission and TraceDecay-owned context compiler
Licensed NCM audit, topology decision, observer integration, then guarded active mode
Feedback, correction, promotion, maintenance, and inspection workflows
Safety, conformance, evaluation, and observer-isolation gates
SDK, host integrations, packaging, and coding-agent journeys

hard_gates.rule: No concrete provider implementation or public provider surface before M1 contracts and conformance model are accepted.
Native remains on the direct path until exact parity evidence and rollback are accepted.
No production NCM transport code before tdmem-0701 and tdmem-0702.
Observer mode cannot affect prompts, canonical state, tools, approvals, or external actions.
Active NCM mode requires scope, stale-memory, crash-recovery, provider-failure, privacy, and observer-isolation evidence.
Every existing upstream-owned file edit requires a current convergence-map entry and must remain within hard patch caps.

no_go_triggers: A provider requires canonical ownership of current code, exact scope identity, sessions, accepted Native facts, curated rules, or final context.
The provider boundary requires direct ProjectMemoryFactStore implementation or shared Native fact tables.
Deadline, cancellation, provenance, exact scope, idempotency, typed terminal outcomes, bounded queues, or recovery cannot reach the concrete provider path.
Observer execution can affect a product-visible output or canonical operation result.
Native parity cannot be proved or rolled back.
NCM licensing or audited surface does not permit a compliant bounded adapter.
Required implementation exceeds the upstream patch budget without an accepted exception ADR.

sign_off.first_action: Implement tdmem-0201 and commit the provider capability registry contract before creating any concrete provider adapter.
